Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style issue resolution beyond Python to multiple programming languages and ecosystems. It tests whether a model can understand unfamiliar build/test tooling and apply language-specific conventions while still producing a correct, test-passing patch.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a larger and generally harder software-engineering benchmark designed to be more industrially representative and more resistant to shortcuts, often requiring deeper repo understanding and longer fix chains. Models must still output patches that satisfy automated checks, but with higher diversity and difficulty than SWE-bench Verified.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic performance in command-line environments, where the model must run commands, inspect files, and iteratively complete tasks under realistic constraints. Success depends on correctly sequencing actions, interpreting tool outputs, and recovering from errors during execution.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp measures deep-research performance using a constrained web corpus or browsing tools, focusing on finding, synthesizing, and justifying answers from sources. Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition

Description: τ2-bench evaluates interactive tool-using agents in simulated real-world service domains (e.g., retail/airline/telecom), where the agent must follow policies while assisting a user over multiple turns. Cognitive Functions:
